clues: For centuries, this condition was heavily linked to 'putrid fevers' that supposedly boiled the blood and sent toxic vapors to the head. As medicine evolved in the 17th century, scientists blamed it on a disruption of animal spirits

Although Hippocrates used about sixteen different words to refer to and name this clinical syndrome such as 'phrenitis' and 'lethargus', the name we currently use derives from latin meaning 'to go out of the furrow'

Up to half of older adults in the hospital experience this. While previously thought to be temporary and harmless, we now increasingly recognize that affected patients face significantly higher short-term and long-term mortality.

Following the American Civil War, northern cattleman noticed that local livestock were dying in droves after coming in contact with healthy appearing cattle from Texas (so called 'Texas Cattle Fever'). Researchers proved that this tiny protozoan parasite was destroying red blood cells and causing the disease. This was the first time that an arthropod was proven to transmit an infectious disease

It's not malaria. The first human case of this was in 1957 where a young cattle farmer fell ill with a high fever, anemia, and ultimately died of kidney failure. He had a prior splenectomy so scientists concluded that this could only affect individuals without a spleen. This was later disproven.
Looking at an infected individual's blood under the microscope, you might see these parasites arranging themselves in a unique tetrad formation that resembles a maltese cross.
In the early 1970s, because of new prescription practices, there was a massive unexpected surge in cases which is now recognized as one of the largest iatrogenic disease epidemics.
In the veterinary world, rabbits are the ultimate outlier for this disease. Up to 60-80% of unspayed female rabbits will develop this after they reach the age of 3-4
Cigarette smoking is oddly linked to a decrease risk of this disease. About 90% of patients first experience abnormal vaginal bleeding leading to early detection.

This was synthesized in 1977 by a Belgian pharmaceutical company that was trying to develop 'nootropics'-- agents that boost memory and cognitive function. However, when it was tested, it failed completely to improve cognition and was shelved for nearly two decades

This drug was approved by the FDA in 1999, despite the fact that nobody knew how it worked. It wasn't until 2005 that researchers finally identified that this medication binds to SV2A, a specific protein wrapper inside neurons
In 2015, this became the first 3D-printed prescription approved by the FDA. It is one of the most widely prescribed anti-seizure medications in the world
The fifth most abundant element in the Earth's crust, this is also the most abundant mineral in the human body

Hyperventilation causes a respiratory alkalosis. This higher pH helps albumin release hydrogen ions creating empty spots for this substance to attach to, which can lead to numbness and tingling in the arms, fingers, toes, or around the mouth

The primary way humans acquire this substance is through diet, but high dietary intake rarely causes high blood levels. If you were to have high blood levels, you might suffer from constipation, kidney stones, confusion, or even arrhythmias.
